race.name: La Épica Gravel Grinder
race.tagline: Two scored gravel stages and an optional criterium on Puerto Rico's hot southern coast.

seo.title: La Épica Gravel Grinder 2027 Guide | Gravel God

vitals.course_status_reason: Organizer-linked 2027 registration confirms a required 170 km Saturday queen stage and a 112 km Sunday circuit stage. The organizer's public route page still shows prior-edition routes, so 2027 elevation, exact gravel percentage, aid locations, and final GPX remain unpublished.
vitals.field_size: Registration cap: 1,500 across all categories; competitive gravel combined field limit: 500
vitals.start_time: Saturday and Sunday competitive fields are listed at 7:00 AM; the optional Friday criterium time is not yet published
vitals.registration: $165 for the competitive two-stage gravel category; online registration closes March 25, 2027 at 5:00 PM ET unless capacity is reached
vitals.prize_purse: Cash prizes are confirmed for competitive categories; amounts are not published
vitals.aid_stations: Rest stops are part of the event, but 2027 locations and spacing are not published

Sunday: 112 km circuit stage, eight laps of 14 km

climate.primary: Hot tropical conditions on Puerto Rico's southern coast
climate.description: NOAA's 1991-2020 Ponce 4 E normals put the March daily maximum at 87.6°F. Prior race reporting adds humidity, mud after rain, and exposed coastal heat to the two-day recovery problem.

terrain.primary: Southern Puerto Rico coastal gravel and mixed backroads
terrain.surface: The organizer describes coastal gravel sectors, agricultural roads, riverside paths, and mixed backroads through Ponce, Juana Díaz, Santa Isabel, and Salinas. Prior-edition reporting adds canal paths, short singletrack, mud, and inconsistent surfaces; the 2027 GPX is not public.

gravel_god_rating.score_note: La Épica earns its score through 282 km of required stage racing, destination terrain, and a real general classification. It remains Tier 3 because the race is young, 2027 climbing and final routes are unpublished, and the broader field and production record are still developing.

biased_opinion.summary: La Épica is not a fondo wearing a timing chip. The competitive product is a two-day general-classification race: 170 km Saturday, 112 km Sunday, and an optional Friday crit that can buy time bonuses. That is a serious weekend. The catch is equally clear: the organizer's route page still describes prior-edition courses, so anyone selling exact 2027 climbing or named sectors is making it up.
strengths: Prior editions produced credible competition and repeat-rider enthusiasm
Hilton Ponce start venue simplifies race-week logistics
weaknesses: 2027 elevation and final GPX are not published
Public route page still shows prior-edition distances
Heat and humidity punish poor recovery
Mainland travel and bike transport raise total cost
Young event with limited long-term field data
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Go for the stage-race format and Puerto Rico, not for a settled course dossier; the required distance is real, the 2027 terrain details are still arriving.

final_verdict.one_liner: A 175-mile Caribbean stage race where Sunday's 112 km starts after Saturday's 170 km bill comes due.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a destination gravel stage race and are willing to train for heat, recovery, and back-to-back volume. Wait if exact climbing and final GPX determine your equipment choice.
final_verdict.alternatives: For a longer established tropical stage race, compare Migration Gravel Race. For a one-day Puerto Rico road target, compare GFNY Puerto Rico.

logistics.airport: San Juan (SJU) has the broadest service and is roughly a two-hour drive; Ponce (PSE) is closer but has limited schedules
logistics.lodging_strategy: Base at or near the Hilton Ponce Golf & Casino Resort, the organizer-listed start venue, and book early enough to avoid daily transfers
logistics.food: Ponce has full dining and grocery options; the organizer has not published 2027 on-course nutrition or exact rest-stop spacing
logistics.parking: Not published for 2027; verify Hilton venue instructions in the final rider guide

eligibility.status_note: Organizer and organizer-linked registration confirm the March 26-28, 2027 event, competitive general classification, two required stages, cash prizes, and registration.

source_review.facts_scope: The mandatory competitive race begins Saturday March 27 with a 170 km queen stage and ends Sunday March 28 with a 112 km circuit stage. Friday March 26 is an optional criterium with general-classification time bonuses. Exact 2027 elevation, GPX, aid spacing, and cutoff remain unknown.
source_review.discovery_note: New relevant race discovered during the August 2026 final-fleet source audit and added under the standing discover-grade-database-page rule.

training_plan_clearance.guard: Calendarize the optional Friday criterium separately, the required 170 km queen stage on Saturday, and the required 112 km circuit stage on Sunday. Use 282 km / 175.2 mi as the confirmed competitive weekend total. Do not claim a 2027 elevation total, exact gravel percentage, aid spacing, cutoff, or named route sector until the organizer publishes the final rider guide and GPX. Prior-edition route reporting may inform general heat, mud, mixed-surface, and recovery preparation only.

history.origin_story: La Épica was built as a multi-day gravel event centered on Ponce and the agricultural and coastal roads of southern Puerto Rico.
notable_moments: The November 2024 edition established the Friday criterium plus weekend stage format
Ted King raced the 2026 edition and finished third overall
The 2027 edition expands the required competitive weekend to 170 km Saturday and 112 km Sunday
history.reputation: A young destination stage race with a serious competitive format and a strong Puerto Rico identity.

course_description.character: Back-to-back gravel stage racing from a Ponce resort base through coastal flats, riverside and canal paths, farms, mixed backroads, and short rougher sectors. The 2027 route geometry is not yet public.

suffering_zones.label: Optional Crit Tax
suffering_zones.desc: Friday time bonuses tempt general-classification riders into high-intensity work before the required endurance stages begin.
suffering_zones.terrain_detail: Short gravel criterium circuit; 2027 schedule pending

suffering_zones.label: Queen Stage Exposure
suffering_zones.desc: The 170 km Saturday stage turns ordinary heat, hydration mistakes, and inconsistent surfaces into Sunday's problem.
suffering_zones.terrain_detail: Coastal gravel, farm roads, and mixed backroads

suffering_zones.label: Eight-Lap Reckoning
suffering_zones.desc: Sunday repeats a 14 km circuit eight times with 170 km already in the legs; pacing and recovery matter more than one fresh-lap speed.

course_description.signature_challenge: Recovering from a 170 km queen stage well enough to race 112 km of repeated circuits the next morning.

guide_variables.race_distance: 282 km / 175.2 miles across two required stages, plus an optional Friday criterium
guide_variables.race_terrain: Coastal gravel, farm roads, canal and riverside paths, mixed backroads, and repeated circuit racing
guide_variables.race_weather: Late-March Ponce climate normals near an 88°F daily maximum, with humidity and rain-driven mud possible

non_negotiables.why: The required race is 170 km Saturday followed by 112 km Sunday, not one isolated long ride.
Ponce's March daily maximum normal is 87.6°F and prior-edition reports describe heat and humidity.
Sunday performance depends on post-stage fueling, cooling, sleep, and bike reset after 170 km.

research_metadata.data_confidence: high for 2027 dates, competitive status, mandatory stage distances, registration, venue, and field limits; medium for terrain character; low for final 2027 climbing and exact route

logistics.explanation: Ponce is a destination for most riders, but a single Hilton start venue and abundant city lodging keep the weekend simpler than a moving stage race.

length.explanation: The required 170 km Saturday and 112 km Sunday total 282 km, comfortably inside the multi-day top score.

technicality.explanation: Organizer and prior-edition reporting describe canal paths, short singletrack, mud, gravel, and mixed backroads without evidence of sustained MTB-only terrain.

elevation.explanation: The southern-coast route includes rolling and climbing terrain, but the organizer has not published a 2027 total; the conservative score avoids importing old-course elevation.

climate.explanation: NOAA gives Ponce a March daily maximum normal of 87.6°F, while prior race reports add humidity and rain-driven mud; challenging, but not automatically extreme.

altitude.explanation: The race is based on Puerto Rico's southern coast and no published 2027 sector reaches altitude that demands acclimatization.

adventure.explanation: Two days across the farms, rivers, coast, and mixed roads of southern Puerto Rico make La Épica destination-worthy without pretending the young event is already iconic.

prestige.explanation: Ted King's 2026 start and the event's international ambition matter, but La Épica is still a young regional race rather than a nationally established fixture.

race_quality.explanation: Timed stages, general classification, category prizes, tracking, a resort venue, and repeat editions show competent production; long-term evidence remains limited.

experience.explanation: A Friday spectator crit and two distinct stage days from Ponce create a memorable race weekend that is larger than a single start-finish transaction.

community.explanation: First-person reporting praises the welcome and Puerto Rico identity, while the event is still building the repeat-rider history required for a higher score.

field_depth.explanation: Cash prizes, open and masters general classifications, and Ted King's 2026 podium support a competitive field, though no complete 2027 roster exists.

value.explanation: $165 for two required stages plus access to an optional criterium is fair for a timed destination weekend, not unusually cheap.

expenses.explanation: Mainland flights, bike transport, a rental car, and Ponce lodging make this a high-cost weekend even though U.S. travelers avoid international formalities.
